value.rationale: The Fourier idempotent of a multiplicative quartic subgroup is a canonical frequency-projection operator, and its sharp endpoint norm is a natural Fourier-algebra invariant, not an arbitrary finite slice. The nonreal-period congruence class is geometrically distinct from the cubic and real-quartic regimes. The closed formula is an infinite-family exact invariant revealing the signed two-squares coordinate, arithmetic dependence of the leading square-root growth, and complete norm-attaining inputs. The classical Gauss algebra is credited; this is a focused exact harmonic-analysis result, not a claimed general Gauss-sum breakthrough.
